title: tests: config + pipeline group filter integration tests
description:
## What
Write integration tests in the transit crate verifying config wildmat validation and pipeline group filtering end-to-end.

## Algorithm
Test file: crates/transit/tests/groups_filter.rs (or extend existing test module)

Test 1 — valid_wildmat_config_loads: Build Config with names=["comp.*", "sci.*", "!alt.binaries.*"] via TOML; call validate(); assert Ok.

Test 2 — all_negation_config_rejected: Build Config with names=["!comp.*"]; call validate(); assert Err containing "positive" in message.

Test 3 — pipeline_accepts_matching_group:
  - Build GroupFilter::new(&["comp.*"]) 
  - Construct minimal article bytes with Newsgroups: comp.lang.rust
  - Call run_pipeline() with ctx.group_filter = Some(filter)
  - Assert PipelineResult::Stored (group log entry created for comp.lang.rust)

Test 4 — pipeline_rejects_non_matching_group:
  - GroupFilter::new(&["comp.*"])
  - Article Newsgroups: alt.test
  - Call run_pipeline() with filter
  - Assert the group log has no entry for alt.test (article IPFS block stored but no log entry)

Test 5 — pipeline_negation_excludes:
  - GroupFilter::new(&["comp.*", "sci.*", "!alt.binaries.*", "alt.test"])
  - Article Newsgroups: alt.binaries.pictures
  - Assert no log entry for alt.binaries.pictures

Test 6 — pipeline_no_filter_accepts_all:
  - ctx.group_filter = None
  - Article Newsgroups: alt.test
  - Assert log entry created (backward-compatible default)

Oracle for all tests: hardcoded expected group names and filter patterns from epic acceptance criteria.

## Defensive programming rules
- Tests use in-memory SQLite (not a real file) to avoid disk state
- Tests use deterministic article bytes with known Message-ID
- No test uses run_pipeline() output as oracle for another test
- Tests run in isolation (no shared state between test cases)

## Agent team
Standard: Agent R (read existing pipeline test helpers), Agent I (write integration tests), Agent V (cargo test -p stoa-transit + clippy)

## Tests
The tests ARE the deliverable. Six named integration tests enumerated above.
